title: Exact Helmholtz boundary representation with actual traces
statement: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded smooth domain, $k>0$, $x\in\Omega$, and let $u$ be a smooth solution of $(-\Delta-k^2)u=f$ on $\Omega$ with $f$ smooth, using the outgoing fundamental solution $G_k$ of the source Helmholtz lemma ([[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]], [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]). Then $$u(x)=\int_\Omega G_k(x-y)f(y)\,dy+\int_{\partial\Omega}\bigl[G_k(x-y)\,\partial_nu(y)-u(y)\,\partial_{n_y}G_k(x-y)\bigr]\,dS_y,$$ with $n$ the outward normal. For an exterior outgoing solution truncated by a large sphere, the same representation holds with the actual inner boundary traces: the outgoing leading terms of $G_k$ cancel the large-sphere Wronskian integrand at leading order and the remaining compact-observation estimate tends to zero. Consequently the identity requires the consistent actual pair of traces $(u|_{\partial\Omega},\partial_nu|_{\partial\Omega})$; assigning both aperture values $u$ and $\partial_nu$ independently is not a well-posed exact boundary prescription, and an expressly adopted scalar aperture-source model is a separate approximation with its own regime of validity.
strategy: Apply the second Green identity ([[cor-second-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]) on $\Omega\setminus B_\delta(x)$ to $u$ and $G_k$. The $k^2$ terms cancel; the unit-flux inner kernel and the continuous limit of $u$ contribute the $-u(x)$ term from $\int(u\Delta G_k-G_k\Delta u)$, while the volume source contributes $\int G_kf$. Letting $\delta\to0$, the derivative-test inner term is $O(\delta)$ and the flux times $u-u(x)$ tends to zero by continuity, giving the displayed formula with the normalisation and outward-hole sign fixed as in the source lemma ([[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]]). For the exterior case, truncate the outgoing solution by a large sphere and use the outgoing radial decay and Wronskian bound of the spherical Hankel lemma ([[lem-em-outgoing-spherical-hankel-dtn-bounds]]): the large-sphere boundary integrand cancels at leading order, and the remaining term at a fixed observation point is $O(R^{-2})\cdot O(R^2)$-free compact estimate tending to zero, so the same representation uses the actual inner traces.
